attribution.note: Marcus's own words to CNN, reproduced in his post.

semantics.note: Present-tense observation of Nvidia's share price against its peak; 'about a third' is a fair rendering of 'a third'.

contract.note: The plain reading (NVDA price vs. all-time high, 30-36.7% band) is fair and ordinary. The rule barring a verdict for unknown accounting basis fits a share price poorly, but the result is unresolved on timing and adjustment grounds anyway.

evidence.note: Stockscan's $166.39 close vs $243.37 high implies ~31.6%, inside the band. But the page's figures conflict, its prices are dividend-adjusted, and the intraday range at the time of the remarks could fall below 30%.

reviews.rationale: One unverified source gives a close that implies ~31.6%, consistent with a third. But the remarks came before the close, the intraday high would imply under 30%, the page's prices conflict, and its adjustment basis differs from the contract's. The packet doesn't settle the figure at the time of the remarks.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words to CNN, reproduced in his post.

semantics.note: 'Gave the market a bounce' credits the reinstatement with causing the rise; 'definitely' is high confidence, not a hedge. Same-day scope kept.

contract.note: Broad indexes and a material (not sole) contribution is a fair, ordinary reading.

evidence.note: Same-day Yahoo report: S&P, Nasdaq and Dow sharply higher, attributed to investors cheering the reinstatement.
AP: futures already pointed to a rebound, and the Huang news then accelerated the rally; all major indexes up. Supports a material contribution.
Broker note names Asian policy steps as other drivers; it does not rule out an added effect from the reinstatement.

reviews.rationale: Major indexes rose broadly on Nov 23. Two contemporaneous reports credit the reinstatement with a material part of the move, and AP says it accelerated a rebound already under way. Other drivers existed, but the claim does not assert sole causation.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words to CNN, reproduced in his post.

semantics.note: 'There's going to be' is a firm forecast. The proposition leaves out the China-chips inconsistency question but keeps the core insider-trading and corruption questions.

contract.note: Independent, broad questioning on both topics is a fair reading of 'all kinds of questions'. No breadth threshold is given, so the judgment rests on interpretation.

evidence.note: Raskin publicly questions motives and financial interests behind the reinstatement push: corruption-type questioning.
Castor explicitly calls the administration's stance corrupt: a second independent voice on corruption.
One analysis flags suspicious prediction-market bets before the announcement. It is a thin basis for broad insider-trading questioning.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was given. Corruption questioning is documented by two lawmakers, but insider-trading questioning rests on a single prediction-market analysis. The early-resolution bar of unmistakably broad questioning on both topics is not met by the cutoff.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words to CNN, reproduced in his post.

semantics.note: 'Is still going to investigate' is a firm forecast that congressional scrutiny continues despite the White House's backing.

contract.note: Counting formal continuation of hearings or interviews as investigation is a fair, ordinary reading; mere calls to investigate are excluded.

evidence.note: Himes statement on Nov 23 says Congress still has questions and expects Huang on the Hill next week despite reinstatement.
Senate Banking notice lists Huang as witness at a Dec 3 export-control oversight hearing, so the process is maintained.

reviews.rationale: Official records dated Nov 23 show congressional investigative processes affirmatively maintained after the reinstatement: the House Intelligence ranking member says they expect Huang next week, and the Senate Banking hearing lists him as witness. This meets the early-resolution rule; the testimony itself is not required.
